title: Amsterdam at Christmas: lights, markets and what's open
author: Brogan
intro: Amsterdam at Christmas is less about big markets and more about canal lights, cosy cafés and the Amsterdam Light Festival. It's cold, often grey and short on daylight, but the evenings are lovely. Here's what's on in 2026, what's open and how to plan it.
seo_title: Amsterdam at Christmas 2026: lights, markets, what's open
seo_description: The Light Festival runs from 26 Nov 2026 to 17 Jan 2027 and Museumplein has a Christmas village in December. Expect about 7°C. What's on and what's open.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Light Festival:** 26 Nov to 17 Jan
- **Christmas market:** Museumplein, December
- **Daytime highs:** about 7°C
- **Best for:** lights and cosy evenings
- **From London:** direct Eurostar or flight

Dates here are for winter 2026/27 and some were still listed as provisional when we checked in November 2026, so confirm them before you book.

sections.heading: Amsterdam Light Festival
sections.text:
The festival is the main reason to go in winter. Artists from around the world install light works along the canals in the old centre, and you can see them on foot or from a boat. The 2026/27 edition is listed as running from 26 November 2026 to 17 January 2027, with the works lit roughly from late afternoon until 11pm.

Walking the route is free. Canal boat cruises along the route are the most popular way to see it and are sold by several operators, so book ahead for weekend evenings.

Tip: go on a weekday evening, or on a boat early in the evening, to avoid the busiest crowds on the bridges.

sections.heading: Christmas markets and ice skating
sections.text:
Amsterdam doesn't have a big traditional Christmas market like Cologne or Vienna. The main one is a Christmas village on Museumplein, by the Rijksmuseum, listed for 3 to 27 December 2026, with food stalls, mulled wine and gifts. There's usually an ice rink on Museumplein too, though listings for this winter give different dates.

If markets are the main reason for your trip, [Cologne](/destinations/cologne) or [Bruges](/destinations/bruges) are better bets. Our [best Christmas markets in Europe](/blog/best-christmas-markets-in-europe) guide compares the big ones.

sections.heading: Sinterklaas, Christmas and New Year
sections.text:
The Dutch festive season runs a little differently from the UK's:

- **Sinterklaas (5 December):** the traditional night for presents in the Netherlands. Sinterklaas arrives in Amsterdam by boat in mid-November, with a parade through the city.
- **Christmas (25 and 26 December):** both days are public holidays. Many shops and some restaurants close or shorten their hours, though the big museums usually stay open. Check opening times for the days you're there.
- **New Year's Eve:** a national ban on consumer fireworks applies from New Year's Eve 2026/27, so expect a quieter night than the famous Amsterdam fireworks of the past. Organised displays may still go ahead, so check what's planned.

Local knowledge: book dinner for 24, 25 and 26 December well ahead. Many Amsterdam restaurants either close or run set Christmas menus.

sections.heading: Weather and what to pack
sections.text:
December highs in Amsterdam are about 7°C and January about 6°C, with frequent rain and wind off the water. It gets dark by around half past four in December, which suits the lights but cuts sightseeing time. Plan museums and markets for the daylight hours and save the canals for after dark.

- **A warm waterproof coat:** rain and wind are more of a problem than frost.
- **Hat, gloves and a scarf:** a boat cruise or an evening on the Light Festival route gets cold quickly.
- **Shoes with grip:** the cobbles and bridges get slippery when wet.
- **Care on a bike:** if you hire one, watch out for wet tram tracks and other cyclists, who won't slow down for you.

sections.heading: Getting there and how long to stay
sections.text:
From London, the direct Eurostar to Amsterdam takes about four hours, and there are short direct flights from most UK and Irish airports. Our guide to [where you can go on the Eurostar](/blog/where-can-you-go-on-the-eurostar) covers the train.

Two or three nights is enough to see the Light Festival, a museum or two and the canal ring. December is busy around the Christmas weekends, so the [quietest time to visit Amsterdam](/blog/quietest-time-to-visit-amsterdam) is the first half of January, when the lights are still on. For more ideas, see [where to go in December](/destinations/where-to-go-in-december) and the [Christmas holidays](/destinations/christmas-holidays) page. If you're torn between Amsterdam and somewhere else, add both to somewhere.party and let the draw choose.

faqs.question: Is Amsterdam worth visiting at Christmas?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you like lights, canals and cosy cafés. It's cold and grey, and the Christmas markets are small, but the Amsterdam Light Festival makes the evenings special.

faqs.question: When is the Amsterdam Light Festival 2026?
faqs.answer: It is listed as running from 26 November 2026 to 17 January 2027. Walking the route is free; boat cruises along it need a ticket.

faqs.question: Is Amsterdam open on Christmas Day?
faqs.answer: Partly. 25 and 26 December are public holidays, so many shops close, but the big museums usually open, sometimes with shorter hours. Book restaurants ahead.

faqs.question: Are there fireworks in Amsterdam on New Year's Eve 2026?
faqs.answer: The Netherlands has banned consumer fireworks from New Year's Eve 2026/27, so there will be far fewer than in past years. Check for any organised displays.
